conversations.answer: It appears that you're using an ES6 export statement in your game.js file, and the environment you're running this script in doesn't support ES6 modules natively. This is why the SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export' error is occurring.There are several ways to resolve this issue:Browsers that support ES6 modules: If you're running your script in a browser that supports ES6 modules (most modern browsers do), you should include your script with type "module" in your HTML file like this:[CODE_BLOCK_0]Then, in your other scripts or HTML files where you want to use the Game class, import it as follows:[CODE_BLOCK_1]Babel: If you're targeting browsers that don't support ES6 modules, you'll need to transpile your ES6 code to ES5 using a tool like Babel.Bundler Tools: If you're using a bundler like Webpack or Rollup, you can configure them to resolve these modules and package them in a format that can be consumed by the browser.If you choose to use Babel or a bundler, you will typically set up a build process that transpiles your code whenever you make changes, so you always have an up-to-date version of your script that's compatible with your target environments.

Instead, the event listeners are being added inside game.js, which should provide better separation of concerns and allow your JavaScript to handle its own logic.In the <script> tag linking to game.js, I added the type="module" attribute. This tells the browser to treat this script as an ES6 module, which allows import and export statements.Remember to check that your server is configured to serve .js files with the correct MIME type (application/javascript), as some servers do not do this by default for files imported as modules.
